prompt: A developer asks which MartiX.Platform APIs are safe to use today. They mention Result<T>, ErrorKind, Problem Details, the MXP001/MXP002 analyzer diagnostics, EF Core Specifications, and reliable events from the Wayfinder blueprint. Explain the current package boundaries, which claims are preview or fixture evidence, and which target-only behavior must be verified before coding.
assertions: Identifies MartiX.Platform as a framework-independent Kernel and keeps hosting, DI, logging, JSON, ASP.NET Core, and EF Core in adapters.
Describes immutable Result/Result<T>/Error/ErrorKind contracts, lower-case owner-prefixed dot-separated error codes, reserved platform. ownership, and MXP001/MXP002 as current analyzer evidence.
Routes Problem Details and exception mapping to the ASP.NET Core adapter and warns not to serialize Kernel Result types directly.
Describes Outbox Messages, Delivery Attempts, and Inbox Receipts as reliable-event primitives with observable at-least-once delivery, not exactly-once transport.
Explicitly says the current bootstrap manifest and source/fixture evidence take precedence over unimplemented Wayfinder blueprint APIs.
